title: One-to-One and Recursive Relationships
summary: Develops one-to-one and self-referential relationship patterns, their foreign-key mappings, and SQL techniques for querying recursive structures.

concepts.title: One-to-one modeling
concepts.summary: A one-to-one relationship links each participating instance to at most one instance on the other side and should be labeled when its meaning is not obvious.

concepts.title: Relationship descriptors
concepts.summary: Descriptors clarify multiple or non-obvious relationships between the same entities.

concepts.title: Choosing foreign-key placement
concepts.summary: Foreign-key placement should reflect mandatory participation and minimize unnecessary nulls while still enforcing uniqueness.

concepts.title: Constraint cycles
concepts.summary: Mutually dependent foreign keys can prevent either participating row from being inserted, so constraint design must consider insertion order and cycles.

concepts.title: Self-referential foreign keys
concepts.summary: A recursive one-to-many relationship uses a foreign-key column that references the primary key of another row in the same table.

concepts.title: Self joins and aliases
concepts.summary: Aliases let a query treat one table as separate logical roles so a row can be matched to a related row in the same table.

concepts.title: Recursive querying
concepts.summary: Recursive structures can be traversed by repeatedly following self-references, using suitable common table expressions where supported.

concepts.title: Recursive cardinalities
concepts.summary: Relationships among instances of one entity can be one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many and require mappings that preserve those cardinalities.
